Exact exponential-generating normalization and binomial convolution.

formal_rows.statement: 7.6, 8.2, 8.3, and 8.4 Newton, tangent, and reciprocal derivative identities
formal_rows.status_and_boundary: Exact formal logarithmic derivative and finite coefficient recurrences in the reduced variable. The displayed `z`-variable tangent scaling is not separately named.
Exact inverse convolution for every unit-constant series over a field.

formal_rows.statement: 9.1 and 9.2 Normalized residue section and triangular inverse
formal_rows.status_and_boundary: Exact manuscript normalization, factorial-rescaled triangular identity, and solved recurrence over a characteristic-zero field.

formal_rows.statement: 9.5, 9.6, and 9.7 Appell realization and exact sparse polynomial
formal_rows.status_and_boundary: Exact finite Appell realization, lowering and translation laws, and the manuscript's sparse sum with only degrees `Nn`. The residue specialization here is `r = 1`.
Exact formal product and coefficient convolution in space and order parameters for the generic zero-constant logarithm family.
Exact finite action on monomials and exact operator inversion on every polynomial of bounded degree; the direct residue inverse corollary is the `r = 1` case.
Exact monicity, exact degree, and `omega ^ m` covariance for block-supported Appell polynomials; residue specialization is `r = 1`.
Exact formal theta series in the reduced variable and exact signed reconstruction from the named reciprocal coefficients.
Exact vanishing at `u = 0`, and at `u = -1` for even `N`; these are the root statements underlying the polynomial divisibility claim.
Exact formal fixed-space and range/covariance characterizations for a primitive root. Holomorphic-domain and pointwise versions remain outside this row.
Exact coefficient encodings for substitution into a sum of two formal variables and for separated products. A bridge to a canonical multivariate substitution API is not asserted.
Exact coefficient-encoded bivariate formal addition law. Pointwise analytic evaluation is outside this row.

Exact rational factorial/Pochhammer normalization and formal-power-series identity. The parameter is rational; the explicit erased parameter multiset, complex analytic summation, and Mathlib regularized-hypergeometric bridge remain outside this row.
Exact coefficient-encoded bivariate formal law, including the carry sign `(i+j)/N`. Canonical substitution and pointwise evaluation remain outside this row.
Exact formal rotational invariance and conjugation-fixed coefficients. Pointwise conjugation, zero orbits, and multiplicity preservation remain outside this row.
Exact `AdjoinRoot` quotient algebras, generator relations, power reductions, and `N`-dimensional power bases for `N > 0`.
Exact identities of formal power series in the quotient algebras. Pointwise quotient-algebra convergence/evaluation and the packaged derivation of prior differential laws are outside this row.
Exact closed signed-shift construction and additive power semigroup for `N > 0`.

formal_rows.statement: 6.4 and 6.5 Companion realization and path entries
formal_rows.status_and_boundary: Exact formula for every entry of every matrix power and exact `J_N^N = -I`, plus the matrix-exponential construction. The exponential-section entry bridge, first-column and trace formulas, characteristic polynomial, and simple spectrum remain outside this row.
Exact matrix-exponential addition, inverse, cancellation, and unit laws. The determinant-one and signed-section entry clauses remain outside this row.
Exact formal differential equation, factorial/binomial coefficient equation, solved recurrence, and initial value; the second sum uses the explicit reindexing `k=q+1`.
Exact `P_(N,1)=r` and exact recurrence-normal forms for `P_(N,2)` and `P_(N,3)`. The manuscript's compact factorial rewrites are not separately proved.

Exact divisibility by `X` for the universal polynomial over `ℚ`, plus a separately defined generic-field polynomial with exact scalar evaluation. A named base-change theorem connecting those two polynomial lifts, or generic-field divisibility itself, remains outside this row.

Exact formal quotient definition and exact factorial/binomial recurrence for the kappa-scaled sequence. The bridge identifying these named coefficients with the full-variable tangent series remains outside this row.
Exact nontrivial formal-germ differential-Bell/Riccati identity. Pointwise analytic validity on the entire zero-free set remains outside this row.
Exact branch-free formal family `Phi_(N,j)^(-r)`, its factorially normalized coefficients, and the `r=1` bridge to the triangular inverse. No analytic logarithm branch is asserted.

formal_rows.statement: 9.4 Residue parameter law, polynomiality, and leading term
formal_rows.status_and_boundary: Exact parameter addition, scalar evaluation, leading coefficient, and exact degree of the honest polynomial lift. Analytic complex powers remain outside this row.

Exact arbitrary-order formal Appell specialization: sparse formula, lowering, translation, joint convolution, monicity, covariance, monomial symbol action, and opposite-order finite operator inversion. The two operator encodings are not yet bridged into the manuscript's single displayed named inverse relation.
Exact polynomial lift and scalar evaluation with degree at most `N*n`, completing the formal polynomial clause of theta reconstruction.
Exact literal polynomial divisibility by `X`, and by `X+1` when `N` is even, for positive coefficient index.
Exact formal logarithmic derivative, Newton recurrence in equivalent antidiagonal indexing, initial value, and `Theta_(N,1)=-(u^N+u)`.

Exact standard Bell generating-function specialization, every reciprocal coefficient, exact polynomial degree and leading coefficient over any characteristic-zero field, and generic-field parameter divisibility. This closes the full formal statement of 7.2; it asserts no global logarithm branch.

Actual entire functions, convergence of the existing formal transfer/signed series at every complex argument, independence of root choices, pointwise finite exponential formulas, iterated derivative expressions, full-period ODEs, and exact initial data. Existence of a basis of the full ODE solution space and the one-step section-to-section derivative identities are not asserted by this row.

Exact analytic Wronskians using actual iterated derivatives: lambda^(N*(N-1)/2) for the ordered transfer family and 1 for the ordered signed family, for N>1. The transfer equality also holds at lambda=0. The proofs derive determinant factorization and constancy; no Wronskian or determinant value is assumed.

Convergent scalar series for each entry of the actual matrix exponential, exact first-column identification with the signed entire sections, every diagonal entry equal to the denominator, and trace=N*denominator. The full off-diagonal entry formula, characteristic polynomial, spectrum, and determinant-one claim remain outside this row.
Exact convergent derivative-series bridge, every signed off-diagonal entry, and the determinant-one identity derived from the actual Wronskian.
Exact characteristic polynomial X^N+1, spectrum equal to the Nth roots of -1, N roots counted with multiplicity, and no repeated roots. No spectral certificate is assumed.

Exact uniqueness and explicit expansion for every entire analytic solution of y^(N)=lambda^N y, with unique coefficients when lambda is nonzero. This is the finite-basis assertion for the entire solution space.
Exact pointwise analytic derivative cycles, including both wraparound cases. The generic bridge derives analytic differential identities from the previously defined formal Taylor coefficients.

Explicit root witnesses and unconditional companion determinant for N>1; exact global bound norm(D_N(z)) <= exp(norm(z)). The order and matching type lower bound in Proposition 11.2 remain outside this row.

Full near-cancellation lemma with universal epsilon=1/2 and C=3/2, including uniqueness, with no strip restriction. Full order-two cosine zero set in integer and positive/negative natural forms, analytic multiplicity one, and exact lattice spacing.
Exact spanning and unique coefficients for every entire analytic solution of y^(N)=-y, in the signed-section basis with its stated initial normalization.

formal_rows.statement: 11.7 Local zero existence and 11.8 leading correction
formal_rows.status_and_boundary: General two-exponential perturbation theorem, proved by the actual logarithmic contraction. Explicit remainder and derivative bounds imply unique local zero, multiplicity one, displacement and quadratic correction bounds. These helper theorems do not assume or prove global exhaustion.

Exact normalized finite sum and actual signed remainder, derivative jets of every order, zero equivalence and strip estimate from stated real-part gaps. The sector-to-strip confinement clause is outside this row.

formal_rows.statement: 11.5 Canonical polygon gap and strip bounds
formal_rows.status_and_boundary: The canonical roots have the precise positive gap gamma_N. The actual signed remainder satisfies the explicit strip estimate for every derivative order. No polygon-gap certificate is assumed. Global sector confinement is outside this row and supplied by rows 62--67.

formal_rows.statement: 5.8 Conjugation, 11.5 disk bounds, and 11.7 local zero strings
formal_rows.status_and_boundary: For every N >= 3, constructs a unique positive real simple zero near every sufficiently large lattice center with exponential displacement. All smallness hypotheses follow from the actual canonical remainder. Also proves conjugation and local lattice assignment. Exhaustion of all large complex zeros, orbit uniqueness and the original-denominator derivative asymptotic remain outside this row.

Actual signed-remainder leading correction has an explicit quadratic envelope error, exactly a constant times exp(-2 gamma_N t). Proves normalized derivative error. Assumes the stated envelope smallness and local zero membership. Does not cover global exhaustion, derivative sign, reality of the displayed correction, or the full original-denominator asymptotic.

Exact Cartesian sector and explicit strip width log(N-1)/(2 sin(pi/N)) for every sector zero; derived finite polygon projection inequalities and one-term normalization. No large-radius or projection-gap certificate is assumed.

Uniform strip smallness is derived from the actual remainder. Every sufficiently large sector zero belongs to a natural-index local disk, is positive real and simple, and is the only denominator zero in that disk.

Actual entire rotation invariance under every Nth root of unity; existence of a rotation into the fundamental sector with a real-part/norm bound; every sufficiently large complex zero rotates into a constructed positive real simple local zero.

Exact frequency norm, rotation of analytic multiplicity and derivative, uniqueness of a unit-modulus positive real rotation, disjoint lattice disks, and global exhaustion using the canonical finite powers of omega. The full sequence/Big-O presentation is not encoded as a single theorem.

Exact product-rule bridge at zeros, quantified relative error for the actual derivative, exact leading modulus (2 sin(pi/N)/N) exp(cos(pi/N) x), and a modulus-ratio error bound. These explicit estimates assume the stated local disk membership and center threshold; signs and the final sequence-level Big-O packaging remain outside this row.
Full argument-sector confinement, exact normalization, and a common positive constant for derivative jets q=0,1,2. Every constant is derived; Y=log(N-1)/(2 sin(pi/N)), R=1, C=4(N-2) exp(2Y).
Full statement for every N >= 2: compact zero sets are finite, large zeros are simple and lie on canonical positive rays, and the exceptional set is finite.
The exact complex series is entire for N > 0. Convergent reindexing proves D_N(z)=Delta_N(z^N); the power substitution preserves analytic multiplicity away from zero.
Finite exceptional reduced zeros, eventual positivity and simplicity for every N >= 2, and the exact positive half-integer squares with multiplicity one for N=2.

Actual choice-defined positive sequences have local and global exhaustion and tail injectivity for N >= 3. The reduced sequence is the Nth power and satisfies the explicit C t_m^(N-1) exp(-gamma t_m) error. Definitions use a documented fallback only before the proved tail. Together with rows 69-70 this covers all clauses of 11.13; the remaining 11.7 assembly is supplied by row 81. Alternating derivative signs belong to 11.8 and are now supplied by rows 82--83.

Actual positive sequences satisfy tau_m ~ t_m and lambda_m ~ t_m^N. Reciprocal real powers are summable exactly for s>1 and N*s>1 respectively, for N >= 3. This row does not assemble the full complex zero multiset, exceptional multiplicities, or the N=2 exponent statement.

A finite lattice-window counting lemma is applied to the actual positive zero tail, giving density sin(pi/N)/pi with uniform bounded error for N >= 3. This row is limited to tails; rows 77--78 supply both full multiplicity-weighted counts.

Reciprocal summability proves compact-uniform convergence and entire analyticity of the genus-zero product over any shifted chosen positive sequence for N >= 3. Its zero set is exactly that sequence. A sufficiently late shift consists of actual simple reduced zeros by row 71. The finite exceptional factor and equality with Delta_N are not asserted.

Actual disk counts sum analyticOrderNatAt over the finite zero set. The original and reduced entire denominators have finite order at every point, so the Nat-valued order loses no infinite multiplicity. Derived finite-weight comparison lemmas retain all exceptional weights.

Constructs a positive simple tail for every N >= 2, including the exact cosine case. Proves injectivity, lattice windows, exhaustive finite root-of-unity orbits, orbit norms and multiplicities. The structure is constructed from the proved zero theorems, never assumed in the final counting results.
For every N >= 2, the actual disk count, including all exceptional analytic multiplicities, differs from (N sin(pi/N)/pi) R by a uniform bounded amount for all R >= 0.

For every N >= 2, the actual reduced disk count differs from (sin(pi/N)/pi) R^(1/N) by a uniform bounded amount for all R >= 0, including exceptional multiplicities. Together with row 77, this fully encodes Theorem 11.14.

The reciprocal-power series over all distinct zeros, weighted by actual analytic multiplicity, is summable exactly for s>1 for D_N and s>1/N for Delta_N, for every N >= 2. Both boundary divergences are included. Finite exceptional sets are removed only through a proved summability equivalence. This fully encodes Corollary 11.15.

Defines the exact complex summands m(z) exp(-s log(norm z)) over every zero. Proves both sharp absolute-convergence half-planes and failure of absolute convergence on and to their left, local uniform convergence by an explicit strip majorant, and holomorphy of both sums for every N >= 2. This fully encodes Theorem 14.2; meromorphic continuation in 14.3 is not asserted.

One theorem supplies a common tail cutoff, positive simple zeros, exponential displacement, unique global orbit/index representation, exact derivative covariance and the original derivative modulus asymptotic with exponential error measured at the actual zero. This fully encodes Theorem 11.7 for N >= 3. The alternating derivative sign in 11.8 is supplied by rows 82--83.

Canonical signed sections and their denominator derivative are real on the real axis. The lattice phase and the exact signed leading derivative factor are proved, including the alternating power of minus one.

formal_rows.statement: 11.8 Full leading correction and derivative sign
formal_rows.status_and_boundary: At the actual named positive zeros, the leading correction is real and the displacement remainder is bounded by C exp(-2 gamma t). The signed derivative relative error is bounded by B exp(-gamma tau); the eventual alternating sign is also proved explicitly. Together with row 82 this fully encodes Theorem 11.8.

The actual cubic remainder, spectral gap 3/2, lattice centers, and correction (-1)^m exp(-3t/2)/sqrt(3) are identified exactly. The actual positive zeros have error bounded by C exp(-3t). This fully encodes Corollary 11.9.

Derives the exponential derivative lower bound at every sufficiently large zero on every symmetry ray. Its inverse positive integer powers dominate every real polynomial weight. No growth certificate is assumed.

A proved Weierstrass criterion for complex coefficients and bounded logarithmic arguments. Includes absolute norm summability, local uniform convergence, entire sums and half-plane holomorphy. The final denominator specialization in row 87 proves the required summability hypotheses.

Defines the exact exp(-s Log z)/(D_N prime(z)^q) series over all actual simple zeros, retaining exceptional simple zeros and the complex derivative weight. For every N >= 3 and q >= 1, proves absolute and locally uniform convergence everywhere and an entire sum. For N=2, proves absolute and locally uniform convergence and holomorphy on Re(s)>1. Logarithms must exponentiate to the zero and have arguments in a fixed bounded interval. This fully encodes Theorem 14.8.

A locally uniform summable majorant on every bounded parameter set proves that exponentially displaced positive sequences have an entire difference of zeta sums. The needed displacement and summability are derived in row 90.

The scaled Hurwitz model is meromorphic on the whole plane, holomorphic off its sole possible pole, with the exact residue. A nonzero residue gives meromorphic order -1. Uses the pinned proved Mathlib Hurwitz theory.

The proved enumeration carries its actual exponential displacement and offset. Its entire correction and finite missing lattice prefix are constructed, and the exact root-zeta identity with the unshifted Hurwitz model is proved.
Both original and reduced zeta sums split into the actual simple tail and the finite exceptional zeros with their analytic multiplicities. The factor N and the scaled parameter Ns are proved.

Constructs both entire corrections, proves equality on the original convergence domains, global meromorphic continuation, holomorphy off the sole pole, meromorphic order -1 at the pole, and both exact manuscript residues. Fully encodes Theorem 14.3.

Defines the actual multiplicity-weighted branched zero series. For logarithms real on the proved positive tail, it agrees with the absolute zeta plus an entire finite correction. Proves global continuation, the same single simple pole/residue, and an entire difference between choices. Intermediate finite-correction claims hold even for arbitrary exceptional complex values. Fully encodes Corollary 14.6.
Proves D4(z)=cos(z/sqrt(2))*cosh(z/sqrt(2)), its exhaustive real/imaginary zero strings, and simplicity of every zero.

Proves both exact zeta formulas in orders two and four with no omitted exceptional zeros. The identity principle proves that the entire corrections constructed in Theorem 14.3 vanish identically. Fully encodes Corollary 14.4.

Constructs the product over every actual reduced zero repeated according to analytic multiplicity, including all exceptional zeros and N=2. Proves countability, reciprocal summability, compact-uniform convergence, entire realization, normalization and exact zero set. Equality with Delta is supplied by row 102.

Factors out every copy of a selected zero; the remaining product is entire and nonzero there. Proves that the complete product and the reduced denominator have exactly the same analytic order at every point.

Removes all quotient singularities using the proved order equality. Constructs a globally entire, nowhere-zero quotient with value 1 at zero, and proves Delta equals the full product times this quotient. Constancy is proved in row 102.

Constructs an entire normalized logarithm of the quotient. Proves a Borel-Caratheodory rigidity criterion from a uniform disk log-norm bound M(R) with M(R)/R tending to zero. The required bound for the actual quotient is derived in rows 100--102, completing Theorem 12.1.

Proves a normalized entire reciprocal proximity bound by Jensen, quotient proximity by division, and a Poisson real-part estimate. These yield rigidity for a factorization with proved sublinear bounds on both entire factors.
Derives the needed growth bounds from actual zero-power summability and the entire denominator estimate. The fixed exponent 3/4 is valid for every N>=2. No quotient-growth certificate is assumed.

The actual normalized quotient equals one. Proves Delta equals the complete multiplicity-indexed product, compact-uniform convergence to Delta, and the original-variable product for D_N. Fully encodes Theorem 12.1.

Proves the logarithmic derivative of the full product and the exact tangent partial fractions, with absolute and locally uniform convergence away from poles. Auxiliary tail-convergence lemmas use Lean total division at poles; the analytic identity is restricted to nonpoles. Fully encodes Corollary 12.7.
Defines moments over all actual zeros repeated by analytic multiplicity. Proves termwise derivatives of the locally uniform resolvent series and the exact factorial-normalized derivatives at zero.
Identifies every positive-index formal kappa coefficient with the actual zero moment and proves the exact Newton recurrence. The logarithm-series clause is supplied by row 109.

Proves the precise factorial-normalized coefficient formula and its convergent Taylor realization as the actual analytic tangent on every zero-free disk in the reduced variable. Fully encodes Corollary 12.9.

formal_rows.statement: 12.10 Reciprocal Bell formula from zero data
formal_rows.status_and_boundary: The named reciprocal coefficient family equals the complete exponential Bell polynomial in the actual zero moments, for all n including zero and every complex parameter r. Fully encodes Corollary 12.10; earlier general-domain complex-power bridges retain their own boundaries.

formal_rows.statement: 12.8 Theta Bell formula from zero data
formal_rows.status_and_boundary: Uses formal ODE uniqueness and the proved kappa/zero-moment identity to derive the exact theta coefficient formula, including the alternating sign and u^(Nm)+u factor. Fully encodes Proposition 12.8 for the named theta coefficient family.

Constructs the logarithm branch normalized at zero on every zero-free disk, proves exp(-L)=Delta, and proves its convergent zero-moment series throughout that disk using Cauchy estimates. Together with rows 104--105 this fully encodes Theorem 12.6. Also proves the convergent resolvent Taylor series.

formal_rows.statement: 11.2 Dominant exponential on a vertex ray
formal_rows.status_and_boundary: Proves finite exponential dominance with an explicit positive projection gap and specializes to the actual canonical signed denominator on a vertex-facing ray. No dominance or lower-growth certificate is assumed.

formal_rows.statement: 11.2 Sharp growth order and exponential type
formal_rows.status_and_boundary: Defines the closed-disk maximum modulus and the standard logarithmic order/type limsups. Proves two-sided maximum-modulus bounds, actual limits for both logarithmic growth ratios, order one and type one for D_N, and order 1/N for Delta_N. Fully encodes Proposition 11.2; imported standard fact 11.1 is not separately formalized or assumed by this proof.

Identifies the actual support function with the manuscript maximum of cosines, proves continuity and nonnegativity for N>=2, and derives the exact periodic tie directions and strict maximizing vertex off those directions.

Derives a uniform positive projection gap on every compact set avoiding the actual tie directions. Proves the normalized dominant-exponential error bound (N-1) exp(-delta r) and eventual zero-freeness there, with one uniform delta and radius. Supplies every dominant-sector clause of Theorem 11.4.

Constructs explicit radii tending to infinity on which the leading conjugate phases align; lower-projection terms decay and the normalized finite sum has a positive limit. This proves the indicator lower bound even at tie directions, without a phase-alignment certificate.

Proves the exact indicator limsup for every angle and every N>=2. Includes the classical formulation along radii where the denominator is nonzero, so the theorem does not depend on Lean Real.log zero. Together with rows 112--114 this fully encodes Theorem 11.4, including uniform compact-sector estimates and eventual zero-freeness.
Actual diagonal operator on l2, norm-summable rank-one expansion, Hilbert nuclear/trace-class characterization, and exact basis and power actions.
Parseval and absolutely convergent double sums prove the operator trace in every orthonormal Hilbert basis, including powers.

Actual finite-compression matrix determinants converge locally uniformly to the reduced denominator; the zero-indexed operator is trace class and every positive power has trace kappa. Specialized diagonal Fredholm theory, with no general operator determinant assumed.
Finite complete homogeneous functions are actual monomial sums indexed by weak compositions; their generating function and Newton recurrence are proved independently of reciprocal coefficients.

Norm-summable eigenvalues give coefficientwise limits of the finite monomial sums. Repeating eigenvalues r times gives the exact positive-integer reciprocal coefficient; the complex-parameter Bell continuation is proved.
The literal normalized factorial series is entire and equals the residue transfer section after multiplication by z^j. Actual Taylor derivatives and value one at zero are proved.
Jensen bounds the actual multiplicity-weighted zero counts of a normalized entire function by its disk growth.
Multiplicity-weighted counting growth implies the exact subcritical power-sum summability bounds, by finite shell estimates.

General normalized entire functions with sublinear power growth equal the complete genus-zero product over their actual zeros with multiplicity. All summability and quotient-rigidity prerequisites are derived.
Global factorial/exponential bounds for the actual normalized sections imply every zero-power summability exponent above 1/N.

Cauchy's estimate supplies explicit Taylor coefficient bounds, Big-O bounds and exact factorial/block rescaling.
The normalized pole has the exact binomial Taylor coefficients. Lower pole orders satisfy a uniform polynomial coefficient bound.

The manuscript's local O(1) principal-part conditions imply nonnegative meromorphic order. The constructed normal-form remainder is holomorphic throughout the required zero-free disk after all finite principal parts are removed.
Actual analytic principal parts have the stated binomial coefficients. Integer reciprocal powers of the signed denominator have exactly the manuscript's factorial-scaled P coefficients.

Derivative rotation and block exponent invariance give N identical contributions per orbit. An equivalence records the chosen representatives and all distinct rotations; the resulting main term retains both proved error bounds.

D_1=exp(-z), T_1=1, and all order-one tangent coefficients are identified. Together with the prior N>=2 theorem, the original-variable tangent series converges with the exact factorial normalization for every positive order.
